package_info.package_manager: Linux ELF binary (malware distributed via shell script, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: Observed in variants since February 2023; current version distributed after mid-April 2023
package_info.why_malicious: AndoryuBot is a botnet malware that exploits a remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2023-25717) in Ruckus wireless devices to gain unauthorized access, propagate itself, establish C2 communication via SOCKS5, and launch DDoS attacks on command. Its behavior is entirely malicious, with no legitimate functionality.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After successful exploitation, the script downloads the AndoryuBot binary for the appropriate architecture, makes it executable, and runs it with a parameter, enabling malware installation and execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated download and execution of a binary from an untrusted remote server is a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal post-exploitation scripts may deploy legitimate updates or tools, but should not fetch and execute unknown binaries from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated deployment scripts in DevOps may download and run trusted binaries from official sources.

execution_context.file_location: AndoryuBot ELF binary (.rodata section, main routine)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Prints: 'Project Andoryu(12/30/2022). What color is your botnet !'
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At process start, the malware prints a unique banner string to the console, indicating successful execution and botnet identity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware often prints unique banners for operator confirmation or anti-analysis signaling.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate binaries rarely print cryptic or botnet-related banners on startup.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some open-source tools print banners for branding.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: GET request to api.ipify.org with hardcoded User-Agent
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At startup, the malware sends an HTTP GET request to api.ipify.org to determine the public IP address of the infected device, using a hardcoded User-Agent string.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware commonly fingerprints the infected host's public IP for C2 tracking or attack targeting.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software rarely needs to determine and report its public IP at startup, especially with a hardcoded User-Agent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Network diagnostic tools may check public IP, but not in malware context.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After initialization, the malware establishes a persistent connection to its C2 server using the SOCKS5 protocol, enabling remote command and control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Persistent outbound connections to hardcoded IPs using proxy protocols are hallmarks of botnet C2 communication.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not connect to unknown external IPs without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: VPN clients or proxy tools may use SOCKS5, but not to untrusted C2 addresses.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Implements 12 DDoS attack methods (e.g., tcp-raw, udp-plain, icmp-echo) triggered by C2 commands
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon receiving a command from the C2 server, the malware launches a DDoS attack using one of several methods, targeting a specified IP and port.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated DDoS attack routines controlled by remote C2 are inherently malicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should never launch network floods or attacks on remote targets.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testing tools may simulate DDoS, but only with explicit authorization.

attack_chain.action: Exploit CVE-2023-25717 to gain remote code execution on Ruckus device.
Download and execute AndoryuBot binary for the device architecture.
Initialize malware, print banner, and decode configuration data.
Determine public IP address of infected device.
Establish persistent SOCKS5 connection to C2 server.
Receive and execute DDoS attack commands from C2.

behavioral_signatures: Post-exploitation download and execution of architecture-specific ELF binaries
Outbound HTTP requests to api.ipify.org at process start
Persistent outbound SOCKS5 connections to hardcoded IPs
Execution of DDoS attack routines on remote command
file_indicators: Shell scripts that fetch and execute binaries from 163.123.142.146
network_indicators: HTTP GET requests to api.ipify.org with unusual User-Agent
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for post-exploitation scripts that download and execute binaries from untrusted IPs, especially those named 'Andoryu*'. Detect outbound HTTP requests to api.ipify.org at process start, and flag persistent SOCKS5 connections to known C2 IPs. Look for processes that implement multiple DDoS attack routines or respond to remote commands. Correlate with known file hashes and network IOCs for AndoryuBot.
